Case study · SaaS · Trades

MeisterMeld: voice-first reports and job management for tradespeople

An AI-assisted field-service app that lets trades businesses create work reports by voice and photo right on the job site – instead of typing up notes in the evening.

Role
Concept, design, development, deployment, operations (sole developer)
Status
MVP live – the first users from the trades are testing the app
Stack
Next.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, PWA, LLM
Operations
Own VPS (1blu), deployment via GitHub Actions
  • Next.js
  • TypeScript
  • PostgreSQL
  • Drizzle ORM
  • PWA
  • LLM
  • Voice-first
  • Field Service

The problem: documentation costs time the job site does not have

In the trades the work happens on site, but the documentation often only afterwards: notes on scraps of paper, photos in the phone, reports at the desk in the evening. That is time nobody can bill – and information gets lost along the way.

The solution: speak first, let the AI structure it

MeisterMeld turns the workflow around. Employees speak the report or upload photos, and an AI (LLM) turns it into a structured work report that the company can review, download as a PDF and attach to the job.

  • Voice and photo uploads as input, AI reports as output
  • Quick report without a job – when something has to be documented fast, without creating a job first
  • Customer, job and employee management in one app
  • PWA: installable on the smartphone, no app store needed

Technology and decisions

  • Next.js + TypeScript for UI and API, PostgreSQL with Drizzle ORM as a typed data model
  • Voice-first and mobile first: the app is built for work on the move, not for the desk
  • Own VPS instead of PaaS: full control over data and operations, hosting in Germany
  • Deployment via GitHub Actions on every push to the main branch
  • Deliberate scope: I do not rebuild accounting and invoicing – specialised programs exist for that. MeisterMeld focuses on what is missing on site: fast, clean documentation.

Lesson from operations: once people work with the app during the day, deployments are no longer an internal matter. Low-downtime releases are part of the product – not just of the infrastructure.

What this project shows

MeisterMeld is the most effort-intensive project in my portfolio because it touches every layer: product idea and UX, AI integration (voice, photo, structured outputs), data model, authentication and roles, deployment and operations with real users.
